subject: Live stream stalls during high-throughput demo — urgent exec action requested
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan.li@novaflow.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novaflow.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime demo: intermittent streaming stalls (high concurrency)

Lauren / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick onboarding earlier today. During the internal load demo we pushed a sustained burst (~1k concurrent websockets) and began seeing repeated 'silent chunk' periods: the stream produces tokens for ~20s and then stalls for 12–45s before resuming. Affected endpoints are /v1/realtime and the websocket streaming path.

Symptoms observed: 
- Clients display indefinite spinner until reconnect or 502 returned by our proxy (we saw 0.4% 502s and ~3% long-tail >10s token pauses).
- Stalls correlate with higher token-per-session workloads (multi-turn assistant flows).
- This started at ~14:45 PST and has been reproducible with the same test harness.

We attached a network capture and the debug logs. We're in a tight window — customer execs are on the phone tomorrow morning and this threatens the go/no-go for the pilot. Can Redwood help immediately with mitigation and executive visibility?

Appreciate urgency —
Megan
Novaflow, Senior SRE

Attachments: novaflow_network_trace_20280103.pcap, novaflow_debug_logs_20280103.zip

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Megan Li <megan.li@novaflow.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jan 2028 15:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: intermittent streaming stalls (high concurrency)

Megan —

Thanks for the detailed reproduction steps and for sending the captures. I'm sorry you're hitting this during the demo window. I've kicked this up to our on-call infra + realtime team and copied Karthik (serving runtime) and Vanessa (CS) so we can coordinate.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Vanessa/Karthik: can you review the pcap and logs and call out obvious proxy/backpressure vs runtime-caused stalls?
- Megan: please confirm if the affected sessions are pinned to a Dedicated pool in us-west-2 and whether you were using a quantized variant (you mentioned gptj-13b-q earlier).

I'll prepare an exec summary and mitigation plan to share with Novaflow leadership within the hour. If we need to pull in product or sales leadership I'll do that.

— Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Megan Li <megan.li@novaflow.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jan 2028 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: intermittent streaming stalls (high concurrency)

Megan / Lauren —

Quick triage from CS side: we see two patterns commonly tied to this behavior: 1) chunked-transfer buffering at the proxy/load-balancer causing delayed forwards, or 2) runtime-level kv-cache/kv-shard saturation leading to token emission pauses.

Immediate mitigations to try now (non-breaking):
- Temporarily reduce concurrency per client to 300–400 and retest (helps identify load threshold).
- Disable per-request prefix-caching (if enabled) to reduce kv-shard pressure.
- If you can, switch to the non-quantized model variant for 30–60m to see if stall frequency changes.

We'll standby to implement a short-lived routing rule (route to fallback pool with higher headroom) if you want us to.

Vanessa
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Megan Li <megan.li@novaflow.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jan 2028 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: intermittent streaming stalls (high concurrency)

Thanks for the captures, Megan — I've pulled the pcap and a preliminary look shows bursts of TCP retransmits followed by long tail ACK delays around the same timestamps as the silent chunks. Two immediate engineering hypotheses:

1) upstream proxy (customer side or partner edge) is coalescing chunked frames which combined with our keepalive cadence causes the client to see silence until the buffer flushes.
2) our runtime is hitting a KV-cache hot-shard under the specific workload pattern (many long contexts plus prefix reuse) which triggers a per-shard stall while we reorder kernel execution.

Planned immediate actions (I can own):
- We'll spin an isolated fallback pool in us-west-2 with increased worker headroom and a lowered batching window to reduce tail latency; route a small percentage of traffic to it (canary) and watch for stall reduction.
- I'll instrument additional per-shard latency sampling and push a short-lived patch that reduces aggressive coalescing inside the runtime for streaming responses.

Can Novaflow attach the exact request headers (including any proxy buffering hints) and confirm whether you're terminating TLS at a gateway that might be buffering? If you can flip a traffic slice to the fallback pool now we can test within 30–45 minutes.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: ops@novaflow.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Jan 2028 16:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: intermittent streaming stalls (high concurrency)

Lauren / Karthik / Vanessa —

Attached: novaflow_network_trace_20280103.pcap and novaflow_debug_logs_20280103.zip. Notes from our infra team: TLS terminates at a L4 gateway (internal) and we have an Nginx-based reverse proxy that sets proxy_buffering on by default. We turned proxy_buffering off for the test harness but may have missed it on a subset of nodes.

We've toggled buffering off cluster-wide and re-ran a small-batch test: stall frequency down from ~3% to ~0.3% but still intermittent at scale. We can route 10% of demo traffic to the fallback pool if Redwood provisions it.

We need a clear mitigation plan prior to our exec call at 9am PT tomorrow. If this is an infra capacity/config mismatch we need to know whether an SLA credit or schedule pause is warranted.

— Novaflow Ops

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Megan Li <megan.li@novaflow.com>, ops@novaflow.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jan 2028 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Live stream stalls during high-throughput demo — urgent exec action requested

Team — quick executive summary and immediate plan for the Novaflow pilot call:

What happened: During a high-concurrency internal demo Novaflow observed intermittent streaming stalls (silent-token windows between 12–45s) and a small % of 502s. Root causes under investigation: a subset of proxy nodes were still buffering chunked frames and our runtime experienced hot-shard kv pressure under the specific workload pattern.

Impact: Pilot go/no-go is at risk for the customer execs tomorrow morning. Observed business impact: degraded UX during multi-turn sessions, brief 502s for a minority of sessions. Estimated revenue at risk: pilot contract (NW-2027-Q4-09) — immediate mitigation reduces risk to acceptable levels for a short demo window.

Immediate actions (next 90 minutes):
1) Redwood will create an isolated fallback pool in us-west-2 and open a short-lived routing rule to move 10% of traffic to it (Karthik).
2) Novaflow will confirm TLS termination and ensure proxy_buffering=off cluster-wide (Novaflow Ops).
3) Redwood will push temporary runtime coalescing reduction (non-invasive patch) and increase per-worker headroom for the fallback pool (Karthik + infra).
4) Vanessa will run the reduced-concurrency test and report stall metrics back in 30 minutes.

Executive escalation: Rafael (cc'd) is aware and standing by to engage commercial leadership if we need a formal SLA credit or to pause the pilot. Lauren will join the 9am PT call and present the mitigation outcomes.

Requested from Novaflow: attach the exact client request headers and a short packet summary for any node still showing buffering. Also confirm whether you want Redwood to perform a brief rollback to the previous non-quantized model variant for the demo window.

I'll update the Jira INF-4321 with the timeline and link to captures. If we see reoccurrence after the fallback routing we'll escalate to the platform reliability incident channel.

— Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_mitigation_playbook_v1.docx
